claim_text: Both insufficient and excessive iodine intake can impair thyroid function; people with pre-existing thyroid disease may be more susceptible to adverse effects from excess iodine, so iodine supplementation should not be inferred from a thyroid diagnosis or symptoms alone.
health_goal_or_outcome: Avoid iodine excess or inappropriate supplementation in people with thyroid disease.

population.age_range: Age- and life-stage-specific intake references apply.
population.sex_or_life_stage: Pregnancy and lactation have distinct iodine requirements and require clinician context.
population.health_status: People with thyroid disease or taking thyroid-active medicines.
population.other_context: Total iodine exposure includes diet, iodized salt, seaweed and supplements.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Iodine supplements, kelp/seaweed products and other iodine-containing preparations.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Iodine Health Professional Fact Sheet describes iodine requirements, thyroid effects of deficiency and excess, and medication interactions.
limitations: A thyroid diagnosis does not establish iodine deficiency.
Kelp iodine content can vary substantially.
Specific thyroid disorders require individualized endocrine guidance.
